items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: Case in point there’s a thing in the new Jazz Times where Gary Giddins is talking about Kenny G... Kenny G supposedly attributes the fact that Charlie Parker got his nickname Bird... I have no problem with him, that’s what he does, it’s music that you can talk over, have in the background.

ctx.x: Would it be safe to say that the melodic part of the African music that filtered into jazz was more of a vocal nature, the way they sang?

Well of course. I mean see the thing is that those vocal things are also a part of the instrumental techniques that were translated. Because it’s a sound in your ear. That’s why © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

a lot of jazz musicians in terms of the academic community would always say oh those jazz musicians play out of tune. Because they don’t recognize it’s coming from a different source. And it’s not going to have that kind of thing because it’s not that type of music in its purest form. So you can’t use that as a barometer to negate or whatever. It’s all music, but all musics have their particular parameters that codify what that music is. So in understanding — and there’s also the argument in the African-American…
